newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Albanian premier appointment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Albanian premier appointment.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday welcomed the appointment of a southerner from opposition ranks to be Albania's new prime minister and repeated its call on rebels in the Balkan state to lay down their arms.
"That's a good step forward," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said of President Sali Berisha's appointment of Socialist politician Bashkim Fino.
"There has been a problem of a south-north divide and if this is a symbolic gesture to try to bring the south and north together, this is a good thing."
The appointment came after news that violence sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes had spread to northern Albania for the first time since insurgency broke out last month.

"We encourage the rebels, the mob, to lay down their arms, and we hope that the opposition and the government can form this national unity government," Burns told reporters in the second such appeal in two days.
Burns said it was "a very serious situation and we're very concerned about it."
Berisha is negotiating with political party leaders in Albania on the formation of a new national unity government to rule until new elections by June.
